transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-28
Start: 14:30 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devin Patel (Redwood SE), Olivia Park (Lighthouse Partnerships), Ethan Ramirez (Lighthouse Partner Sales), Sofia Li (Lighthouse Channel Ops)

Summary (auto): quick pipeline check; prioritize two pilots; align on who owns customer intro & RACI; schedule bench/tech run; share deck/pricing.

00:00 - 00:27 Maya (Redwood): All right, hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Happy holidays again, we're trying to squeeze one more call in before the new year. I'll hand over to Olivia to kick off - high level where you're at and any urgent changes.

00:28 - 01:05 Olivia (Lighthouse): Yeah hi, thanks Maya. Um, quick update - we've had some movement on the healthcare account, Starlake Health, they want a pilot by mid-Jan, looks like they're leaning toward a private deployment, uh, air-gapped type requirement may be a blocker but we can scope.

01:06 - 01:42 Ethan (Lighthouse): And from sales side we've got two more cloud-native deals that are earlier stage but good fit for Redwood Hosted API - they're sensitive to latency though.

01:43 - 02:10 Maya (Redwood): Cool, that's helpful. So for Starlake Health, when you say private deployment, do you mean VPC or on-prem on their side?

02:11 - 02:40 Olivia (Lighthouse): They said "on-prem" a few times, regs and data residency, they have a K M S and H S M setup they need to leverage.

02:41 - 03:12 Devin (Redwood SE): Okay that's doable; Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations and an on-prem package. We'll need to schedule an architecture call - I suspect their infra team will want to validate networking and firewall rules. Also note there are perf trade-offs for fully air-gapped POCs, like we lose some of our smart routing and cache efficiencies.

03:13 - 03:55 Olivia (Lighthouse): Understood. What's the typical uplift if we move from hosted to dedicated to private in terms of implementation time and cost?

03:56 - 04:22 Maya (Redwood): Ballpark, hosted is fastest, dedicated takes a few weeks longer for capacity and config, private can be 4-8 weeks depending on on-prem readiness. Cost varies — we'll share a pricing worksheet.

04:23 - 05:00 Ethan (Lighthouse): One ask: can Redwood provide a short doc on SSO/SAML S S O integration steps for our security team? That usually unlocks the enterprise proc.

05:01 - 05:30 Maya (Redwood): Yes, we'll send the SSO/SAML guide and SOC 2 summary. I'll attach security pack to the deck.

05:31 - 06:10 Sofia (Lighthouse): On co-sell process - we want clarity: who owns the primary commercial relationship post-intro, and how do we message the revenue split to our execs?

06:11 - 07:00 Maya (Redwood): Good q. Our default is partner-led introductions with Redwood owning the technical deliverables and support SLAs for hosted/dedicated; revenue share is negotiable per pilot, we can propose a standard come-in rate for pilots (Maya: will draft). We'll put that in the partner pricing worksheet.

07:01 - 08:05 Olivia (Lighthouse): Great. Also, can we confirm Redwood will run a proof-of-value benchmark — latency and cost per 1k tokens — for the cloud-native deals?

08:06 - 09:00 Devin (Redwood SE): Yes, we can run benchmarks. For the cloud deals we'll test with Redwood Hosted/managed variants and also a Dedcated pool scenario to show cost/latency delta. Note: transcription - Dedcated spelled wrong in some notes but that's Dedicated. We'll include KV cache / prefix cache configuration in the plan.

09:01 - 10:15 Ethan (Lighthouse): Perfect. For the two pilot accounts we think priorities are Starlake Health (on-prem) and Meridian Financial (cloud native). Starlake is highest ARR but longest procurement, Meridian is smaller ARR but faster to get a pilot.

10:16 - 11:10 Maya (Redwood): Sounds like a classic tradeoff. Recommend running parallel workstreams: quick Hosted POC for Meridian to show immediate value and start the procurement conversations for Starlake's Private engagement. That gives you momentum.

11:11 - 12:00 Olivia (Lighthouse): Agree. Question on success criteria - what metrics should we present to customers post-POC?

12:01 - 13:00 Devin (Redwood SE): We usually present latency P95, cost per 1k tokens, throughput (concurrent requests), and quality regression checks vs baseline prompts. Also log/audit review for compliance. We can formalize an eval template.

13:01 - 14:10 Sofia (Lighthouse): On the topic of audit logs and retention, Starlake needs 7 years retention for certain records. Is Redwood able to support extended retention in Private?

14:11 - 15:00 Maya (Redwood): Yes, Private can be configured to meet long-term retention; for hosted we'd need an add-on and it's less common but possible. We'll flag that in the security pack.

15:01 - 17:00 Olivia (Lighthouse): OK good. Next, on commercials — can Redwood accept a partner referral fee or do we need a reseller agreement?

17:01 - 18:00 Maya (Redwood): We support both. For enterprise pilots we often do a reseller-style contract or an MSA addendum. I'll coordinate with legal and send a templated partner addendum.

18:01 - 20:00 Ethan (Lighthouse): For our forecast, we want to put three deals in Q1 — Meridian, Starlake, and Altura Health. Can Redwood commit to quick-turn pricing for Meridian if we can get an intro this week?

20:01 - 21:10 Maya (Redwood): If you get the intro this week, yes we'll prioritize a pilot quote and can front-load resource for a condensed timeline. I'll note that in the action items.

21:11 - 24:00 Devin (Redwood SE): I want to call out technical risks for Starlake: on-prem environment means limited access to instrumentation and we may need a staging cluster on-prem to run KV cache patterns. Also have to confirm their GPU availability or whether we will ship hardware.

24:01 - 26:10 Olivia (Lighthouse): They are willing to host, but not purchase hardware up-front; they'd prefer Redwood-managed hardware in their DC or a co-located dedicated option.

26:11 - 28:00 Devin (Redwood SE): Ok that's workable - that means Redwood Dedicated or private managed option. We'll prepare an architecture options doc.

28:01 - 30:00 Maya (Redwood): Quick pipeline review now — Olivia can you run through the list and status?

30:01 - 32:00 Olivia (Lighthouse): Sure: Meridian Financial - demo complete, trying to get PO in Jan, priority 1. Starlake Health - security review ongoing, legal 4-6 weeks, priority 1 but long. Altura Health - discovery scheduled Jan 6. Acme Retail - low priority, needs edge latency.

32:01 - 34:00 Ethan (Lighthouse): We also have a strategic telco account, HelioCom, that may want a hybrid model (dedicated + hosted fallback) — they asked about automatic fallback to hosted if local capacity is saturated.

34:01 - 35:30 Devin (Redwood SE): Yes, Redwood supports smart routing and fallback policies — we can set policy thresholds for latency or capacity and route to hosted variants; there's an Ops playbook for that. I'll attach the routing playbook link.

35:31 - 37:00 Sofia (Lighthouse): On reporting - can we get per-route cost breakdowns for the pilot so we can allocate spend by account?

37:01 - 39:00 Maya (Redwood): Yup, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost and latency dashboards per model/route; we can configure shared dashboards for Lighthouse.

39:01 - 41:30 Olivia (Lighthouse): A couple of asks: 1) joint exec one-pager for each pilot 2) prioritized contact list and 3) pricing guidance for pilot vs committed Dedicated engagement.

41:31 - 42:30 Maya (Redwood): We'll deliver the one-pager template and the pricing guidance; see action items.

42:31 - 44:00 Ethan (Lighthouse): Any blockers on Redwood side for running a security/arch review with Starlake next week?

44:01 - 45:10 Devin (Redwood SE): We can do an initial scoping call; prefer Jan 7 or 8 for an architecture deep dive — need their infra/engineering folks.

45:11 - 46:00 Olivia (Lighthouse): I'll check with Starlake and confirm.

46:01 - 48:00 Maya (Redwood): Great. Final quick topic — attribution and CRM process: Olivia, we'd like Lighthouse to create the opportunity in your CRM and tag Redwood as partner; also add expected close date so we can align forecasting.

48:01 - 49:10 Olivia (Lighthouse): Sure - will create opportunities this week; will include Redwood contact and expected dates.

49:11 - 51:00 Maya (Redwood): Awesome. Recap of next steps: I'll send the partner deck + security pack + pricing worksheet; Devin will send benchmark plan and routing playbook; Olivia will send prioritized accounts and contact list and confirm POC dates. We'll meet again week of Jan 11 for tech deep dive and pipeline check. Any other items?

51:01 - 51:45 Olivia (Lighthouse): No, that's it. Thanks everyone. Happy holidays.

51:46 - 52:00 Maya (Redwood): Thanks all, talk soon.
